text:
sam: Quick sync — I'm putting up a prototype to auto-capture nsys/perfetto traces in our nightly CI focused on kernel selection + KV cache warmstart regressions. I sketched a workflow, want feedback before I wire it into the nightly job.

lex: SGTM, what's the capture trigger? full nightly or only when latency diff > X?

sam: Plan: always run lightweight smoke profiles every night (fast tiny dataset) + deeper capture when the smoke run shows >5% p50 token latency regression vs baseline commit. Reason: cheap constant coverage + targeted heavy traces only for suspicious commits.

maya: How do you compute the baseline? single commit or moving window? need to avoid flapping.

sam: Using a rolling baseline: median of previous 7 nightly smoke runs per model variant and sequence-length bucket. That smooths noise. We tag baseline by model/version + quantization profile + kernel hints.

chris: For the heavy capture, do we dump full .nsys or a trimmed perfetto timeline? storage could explode.

sam: Idea: capture both but compress/trim: full .nsys kept for 7 days, perfetto JSON timeline + flamegraphs stored long-term. Use selective timeframe capture: focus on the token generation steady-state window (skip model load & init). Example nsys CLI:

```bash
nsys profile --output=/tmp/trace --capture-range=cpu:begin,end --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --force-overwrite --duration=120s your_inference_test.sh
```

sam: Then convert to perfetto for timeline UI and extract kernel-level summaries (kernel name, duration, SM utilization).

lex: How do we associate traces with the exact request workload so kernel selection decisions are reproducible?

sam: We bake a tiny deterministic prompt corpus (committed in repo) and record RNG seeds + batch sizes. Also snapshot the runtime config: batcher policy, kv-cache warmup steps, max_seq, quantize flags. We'll attach a small JSON manifest with each artifact.

maya: KV cache is tricky — warm vs cold paths look different. We should capture both a cold-run trace and a warmed-run trace per job. Cold-run = first token generation after model alloc, warmed-run = after N prefix tokens.

chris: Good call. Maybe N=64 and samples=3 per model variant. That gives us consistent kernel timelines for both paths without too many runs.

ci-bot: @ci-bot triggered nightly perf smoke job for model: 'redwood-large' at commit: abc1234. Artifacts: smoke-stats.json.

sam: Storage policy: compressed perfetto + summary CSV -> long-term s3 (30d cheap tier), full .nsys -> short-term scratch s3 with lifecycle delete 7d. Use object tags: model, commit, seq_bucket, cold/warm, job_id.

lex: For the diff dashboard — what's the metric set? p50/p95 token latency, kernel time split (matmul, softmax, memcpy), SM util, occupancy, warp stalls. Also include kernel-selection decisions log (which kernels were chosen per layer).

sam: Exactly. We'll store a lightweight YAML of kernel-selection fingerprint per layer so the dashboard can show when a layer flipped from cuBLAS->custom-kernel. We'll render regression alerts if any kernel's cumulative time increases >15% and p50 increases >5%.

maya: How do we gate PRs? Do we block merges on these perf regressions? can be noisy.

sam: Proposal: keep nightly alerts only for now. For PRs, add optional per-PR profiler that captures traces on demand (via comment /run-nightly-profiler). If it flags a regression, it posts a summary to PR and creates a perf issue. Later we can decide on blocking merges.

chris: Implementation detail: we need a small agent on the runner to collect GPU metrics (nvidia-smi sampling + nvtx injection). Also integrate with our trace harvester to upload artifacts and kick diff job.

infra-bot: infra-bot note: ensure runners have 1) nsys v2023.x, 2) perfetto converter, 3) 40GB scratch + gzip. Marked image: runtime-perf-capture:stable.

sam: I'll draft the GitHub Action / Jenkins pipeline steps. Rough steps: 1) run smoke profile -> produce smoke-stats.json 2) compare to rolling baseline -> if pass skip heavy traces 3) if fail, run cold/warm nsys captures for configured variants 4) upload artifacts + manifest 5) run diff analyzer -> update dashboard & alerting.

lex: For the diff analyzer, use deterministic bucketing: layer names + kernel fingerprint. Also produce a small HTML with flamegraphs per kernel.

maya: Can we also capture kernel launch parameters (grid/block) from traces? that'll help debug selection heuristics.

sam: Yes — nsys and perfetto export those fields. We'll include a parsed 'kernel_launchs.csv' with (kernel_name, grid, block, sm_util, time_ns).

chris: One more: annotate traces with git metadata + Docker image digest so we can exactly repro.

sam: Will do. I can open a PR with the action + harvester hooks by EOD tomorrow. Any blockers?

lex: No blockers from me. pls include a small README for oncall so they know how to fetch the full .nsys within retention window.

maya: Add a small regression triage playbook too (where to look first: kernel flip table, KV cache hit ratio, batcher histograms).

sam: Great notes — I'll include both. Thanks! :thumbsup:
